nodes.name: foundation_division_exists_unique
nodes.summary: G001: construct the quotient and strict remainder for every nonzero divisor and prove the pair is literally unique.

nodes.name: foundation_signed_bezout_canonical_gcd
nodes.summary: G002: every pair, including (0,0), has a canonical gcd value and actual signed-natural Bezout coefficient codes. Only the gcd is asserted unique, not its coefficients.

nodes.name: foundation_coprime_product_divisor
nodes.summary: G003: coprimality and a witnessed divisor of the product construct an actual quotient of the other factor, with no positivity premise added.

nodes.name: foundation_prime_factor_list_exists
nodes.summary: G004: every positive natural has a genuinely constructed finite beta-coded prime-factor list and actual product trace; the existing sorted construction is used only to obtain witnesses, not required as a premise.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_below_zero_impossible
nodes.summary: There is no natural index below zero; empty list and permutation contracts are genuinely vacuous.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_prefix_reflect
nodes.summary: Actual beta functionality turns a finite forward entry preservation into reverse preservation at every original index.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_all_prime_entry
nodes.summary: Every actual decoded entry of an all-prime prefix is prime, without a supplied choice of matching factor.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_product_exists
nodes.summary: Construct an actual product value and trace for every finite beta prefix, including empty prefixes.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_cancel_last
nodes.summary: Cancel an actual final prime factor, retaining the nonzero predecessor product and all actual prime prefix entries.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_successor_decompose
nodes.summary: Every nonempty prime factorization supplies an actual last prime, its actual quotient, and a genuine shorter factorization.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_unit_length_zero
nodes.summary: The only prime factorization of one has empty length; this is an actual-product statement, not a convention imposed on a list.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_prime_member
nodes.summary: An actual prime divisor is found at an actual occurrence of every unordered prime factorization of the product.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_empty_matching
nodes.summary: The actual literal zero beta code is a bounded/injective/surjective matching permutation between any two empty factor prefixes.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_index_extend
nodes.summary: Append the fresh top index to any actual finite permutation, construct the new beta code, and prove all three bijection conditions.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_matching_append
nodes.summary: A matching map stays matching when the same actual last factor is appended to both lists and the fresh last index is appended to the map.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_matched_append
nodes.summary: Construct a genuine matching permutation after adjoining the same last factor, retaining the exact prefix-preservation and fresh-index equations.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_matched_append_exists
nodes.summary: Existence-only append interface still returns an actual fully bijective matching beta map.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_swap_reflect_unchanged
nodes.summary: An actual swapped prefix reflects back to the original entry at every index other than the two moved indices.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_swap_bijection
nodes.summary: Swapping two actual map entries preserves boundedness and injectivity and constructively recovers full finite surjectivity.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_swap_all_prime
nodes.summary: A genuine index swap retains every prime factor, including duplicate equal primes; no distinct-factor hypothesis is required.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_swap_factorization
nodes.summary: The swapped prime list has an actual product trace with the identical nonzero product, not merely a proposed rearrangement equality.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_swapped_factorization_exists
nodes.summary: Construct a full recoded prime-factor list moving a selected interior prime to the last position, with exact swap witnesses and an unchanged actual product.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_matching_unswap
nodes.summary: Undo a target-list swap by swapping the two corresponding actual source-map entries. Entry alignment follows at the two moved positions and everywhere else by map injectivity.

nodes.name: factor_permutation_matched_unswap_exists
nodes.summary: Use the recursively constructed finite permutation's actual preimage, construct both extended and transposed map codes, and return a full matching bijection into the original unswapped target list.

nodes.name: prime_factor_lists_matching_by_length
nodes.summary: Full induction on an arbitrary source factor list: locate the last prime in the arbitrary target, genuinely swap and cancel it, recursively match the shorter lists, and construct the restored index bijection. Neither list is assumed sorted or distinct.

nodes.name: prime_factor_lists_permutation_exists
nodes.summary: Exact G005: every two arbitrary unordered prime factorizations of the same positive natural admit an actual coded matching bijection, with equal lengths and explicit boundedness, injectivity, and surjectivity.

nodes.name: prime_factorization_exists_unique_up_to_permutation
nodes.summary: Construct an actual prime-factor list for every positive natural and an actual matching permutation to every competing unordered factorization. Both factor-list existence and uniqueness witnesses are conclusions, with no supplied canonical factorization.

nodes.name: SignedDecode
nodes.summary: The original canonical integer code: even 2p denotes p, and odd 2k+1 denotes −(k+1). The decoded positive and negative parts are normalized.

nodes.name: SignedBalance
nodes.summary: The original canonical code z represents the integer difference p−n; these supplied components need not be normalized.

nodes.name: SignedAdd
nodes.summary: Actual addition of original canonical signed codes, witnessed by their decoders and balanced equality.

nodes.name: SignedMul
nodes.summary: Actual multiplication of original canonical signed codes; opposite-sign products remain on the negative side of the balance.

nodes.name: SignedNegate
nodes.summary: Canonical signed negation swaps the positive and negative decoded parts.

nodes.name: SignedBezout
nodes.summary: The original signed coefficient codes u and v witness a·u+b·v=g by actual decoded balanced arithmetic.

nodes.name: Lt
nodes.summary: Witness-defined strict order on natural numbers.

nodes.name: BetaAt
nodes.summary: x is the bounded beta-decoded value at index i.

nodes.name: BoundedPrefix
nodes.summary: Every decoded entry below l is itself below l.

nodes.name: InjectivePrefix
nodes.summary: Equal decoded values below l have equal indices.

nodes.name: SurjectivePrefix
nodes.summary: Every value below l occurs at an index below l.

nodes.name: PermutationPrefix
nodes.summary: An actual beta-coded bijection of the finite index interval [0,l), including all bounds, injectivity, and surjectivity.

nodes.name: Product
nodes.summary: z is the product of a beta-coded prefix of length l.

nodes.name: Prime
nodes.summary: p is nonunit and every factorization of p has a unit factor.

nodes.name: AllPrime
nodes.summary: Every decoded factor below l is prime.

nodes.name: PrimeFactorList
nodes.summary: A positive number n, an actual length-l beta product equal to n, and prime entries. No sortedness or supplied canonicalization is required.

nodes.name: FactorListMatching
nodes.summary: Each actual source factor equals the factor at the index decoded from its image under the witnessed map.

nodes.name: PrimeFactorListPermutation
nodes.summary: Equal list lengths and an actual bounded, injective, surjective beta index map matching all source and target prime occurrences, including repetitions.

nodes.name: DivRem
nodes.summary: q and r are a quotient and a strict remainder for n by d.

nodes.name: Dvd
nodes.summary: The natural number d divides n.

nodes.name: IsGCD
nodes.summary: g is a common divisor divisible by every common divisor.

nodes.name: Coprime
nodes.summary: Every common divisor of a and b is one.
